standard_prerequisites: Context span 746-771, first paragraph: R = k[t], I = (t), P = K = direct sum over N of R, M = direct sum of R/(t^n); the short exact sequence 0 -> K -> P -> M -> 0 with first map multiplication by t^n on the nth summand; after completion, xi = (t^2, t^3, t^4, ...) in P^wedge maps to zero in M^wedge but is not in the image of K^wedge -> P^wedge since that would be the image of (t, t, t, ...) which is not an element of K^wedge

Context, second paragraph: in the situation of Lemma noncomplete-quotient (delivered card L48305) the short exact sequence 0 -> J -> R -> R/J -> 0 does not remain exact after I-adic completion: with f a generator of J the map R -> J^wedge is surjective with image of J^wedge -> R equal to (f) = J, but R/J noncomplete means the kernel of the surjection R -> (R/J)^wedge is strictly bigger than J (Algebra, completion-generalities and quotient-complete); by the same token R -> R -> R/(f) -> 0 does not remain exact on completion
core_obligations: The k[t] example shows completion is not exact in the middle of a short exact sequence: xi lies in the kernel of P^wedge -> M^wedge but outside the image of K^wedge -> P^wedge, so completion is not left exact in general

The situation of lemma-noncomplete-quotient shows completion is not right exact: the surjection R -> R/(f) completed has kernel strictly bigger than the completion of J, so R^wedge -> R^wedge -> (R/(f))^wedge -> 0 is not exact
In both examples I = (t) is finitely generated; in the second the modules R, J and R/(f) are finitely presented, covering the finitely-presented refinement stated in the lemma
proof_roadmap: Read the failure of middle exactness off the k[t] example in the context
Read the failure of right exactness off the lemma-noncomplete-quotient situation in the context
Note the finitely generated ideal and finitely presented modules in the second example
